Import cohort data

a02_import.Rmd

Import the configured study

getDataForStudy() retrieves the cohort records, cleans their intervals and saves the input for trajectory generation. It needs the study environment returned by cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(). See configuration if you have not created one.

CDM data

For a study configured with useCDM = TRUE, pass the connected CDM reference:

getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)

With a non-NULL baseUrl, the package downloads the selected cohort definitions from the ATLAS WebAPI. CDMConnector then generates those cohorts on the supplied database and retrieves their records. ATLAS supplies definitions, not patient data. atlasTargetCohort and atlasStateCohorts refer to definition IDs, not rows in a previously generated cohort table.

The target definition is stored as JSON/0.json. State definitions use JSON/atlas_<id>.json. The package creates CohortsToCreate.csv to map files to generated cohorts. Clinical labels are kept separate from these filenames.

Use local cohort JSON instead of ATLAS

Set baseUrl = NULL and supply filenames without .json. Paths are relative to the study’s JSON folder. For this example, place target.json, states/A.json and states/B.json under local-json/JSON after configuration. They must contain the cohort expressions used to generate the cohorts.

studyEnv <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "local-json",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  useCDM = TRUE,
  baseUrl = NULL,
  atlasTargetCohort = "target",
  atlasStateCohorts = c("states/A", "states/B"),
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)

# Place the JSON files in the study folder before this call.
getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)

The package still generates cohorts on the CDM. Only the source of their definitions has changed. Relative subfolders are supported. Do not use absolute paths or parent traversal in definitions intended for saved replay.

CDM imports work in a temporary JSON folder. Downloads and the new manifest are published only after a successful import. Failed downloads, queries and empty eligible cohorts leave the previous working definitions unchanged. Unrelated JSON files are not replaced.

Local data

Set useCDM = FALSE to import a data frame or CSV without a database. Use these four column names exactly:

Column Content
subject_id Patient identifier. Use character values for leading zeros or large IDs.
cohort_definition_id Character label. "0" identifies a target interval. Other values are state labels.
cohort_start_date Interval start, as an R Date in a data frame.
cohort_end_date Interval end, as an R Date in a data frame.

For CSV input, write dates as YYYY-MM-DD. Dates must be present and the end must not precede the start. Intervals include both endpoints. Patient IDs must not be missing or blank. Numeric whole-number and integer64 IDs are also accepted, but use character or integer64 before creating values at or above 2^53 to avoid rounding in R doubles.

The target label is the text "0", regardless of the clinical labels. This example includes a second patient with a target interval and no state records:

rawData <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("001", "001", "001", "002"),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "A", "B", "0"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-08", "2020-01-01"
  )),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-21", "2020-01-07", "2020-01-14", "2020-01-21"
  ))
)

studyEnv <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "local-data",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = rawData,
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)

getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv)

To configure a CSV source instead, omit trajectoryDataObject and supply pathToData = "path/to/input.csv". The package reads patient IDs and state labels as text, preserving leading zeros and the literal label "NA".

Replace the input for one import

An explicit local source takes precedence over the configured alternative:

# Use this CSV even if the configuration contains a data frame.
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv, pathToData = "path/to/new-input.csv")

# Use this data frame even if the configuration contains a CSV path.
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv, trajectoryDataObject = newData)

Do not supply both non-NULL sources in one call. With neither supplied, the configured data frame is used when present, otherwise the configured CSV is used. Set trajectoryDataObject = NULL in an import call to use the configured CSV instead. These overrides apply to that import only. CDM imports ignore both local source arguments.

What cleaning does

Only patients with a target row are retained. If a patient has several target intervals, the first interval by start date supplies the bounds. State records before its start are removed or clipped. By default, records after its end are also removed or clipped. outOfCohortAllowed = TRUE allows retained state records to extend beyond the target end, without moving the target start.

Overlapping records for the same patient and state are combined. Every label in stateCohortMandatory must occur within the retained interval. This checks presence anywhere in that interval, not eligibility on Day 7. Use NULL or character(0) when no state is mandatory. Patients with only a target interval remain eligible when no mandatory rule excludes them.

When mergeStates = TRUE, overlaps between different states are then represented by their structured membership. Import does not infer diagnoses, prior history or clinical meaning from the state labels.

If no eligible patients remain, import does not succeed. Previous cleaned files are kept, and trajectory generation is blocked until a later import succeeds. Changing mandatory-state requirements also requires another import.

Saved studies

Restore a version 4 snapshot with runSavedStudy = TRUE, then import fresh data. See saved-study configuration for the Settings-only sharing workflow. A saved CDM study uses the definitions embedded in the RDS file, without an ATLAS connection or working JSON files:

getDataForStudy(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = savedStudy)

For a saved local-data study, configure useCDM = FALSE and supply a new local source. The same per-call source precedence applies. Saved runs restore their analysis settings, so do not pass replacement labels, mandatory states, transition rules or merging options.

After import, continue to trajectory generation. The output article describes cleaned data, trajectories and the saved settings file.
